letters.title: January / February Update
letters.excerpt:
Dear Praying Friends,

The first two months of the year have been full — full of travel, full of meetings, full of snow… and full of God's faithfulness.

January Highlights

It has truly been a joy traveling. One of the unexpected blessings of deputation is not just visiting pastors and churches, but reconnecting with dear friends in the ministry. The fellowship along the way has strengthened our hearts more than we can say.

We were privileged to visit several wonderful churches throughout New England. Being close to home allowed me to go soul winning with a good friend, and we were able to see two individuals make professions of faith. There is nothing like watching God work in someone's heart.

During the second week of January, I attended a church planting conference in Oklahoma. The Lord used that meeting to deeply encourage and steady my spirit. It was a timely reminder that the work we are called to is God's work — and He is faithful to build His church.

The third week of January, our family traveled to North Carolina to present the ministry in a couple of churches there. We made it home just before the first major winter storm hit. Praise the Lord, none of our meetings were canceled! We were snowed in Monday and part of Tuesday, but it gave us unexpected family time together.

February Highlights

February kept us in New England the entire month, which allowed for a slightly slower pace and some much-needed rhythm for the kids' sleep schedules.

We were especially grateful to be home for Valentine's Day. Leah and I decided to make pasta from scratch — fettuccine Alfredo. Let's just say… Leah was "in charge" and I was the enthusiastic assistant. (It is clear that church planting may be my calling — cooking is not!) It was a sweet time together.

We were also able to connect with other families. I joined a few dads for fellowship while our wives enjoyed some kid-free time together. It is a blessing to have meaningful fellowship so close to home during this season.

Another snowstorm came through, but once again the Lord protected our schedule. No meetings were canceled, and when we were snowed in, we were safely at home.

Later in the month, I attended a church planting conference in Memphis with a strong emphasis on reaching Black America. It was an incredible opportunity to meet pastors and leaders burdened for inner-city church planting. The connections made there will be invaluable as we prepare for Bridgeport.

A Special Provision

We also had to find a new doctor recently, and the Lord provided immediately. Leah found a practice run by believers that accepts our insurance. Adalee and Anthony had their first appointments, and we were so grateful for the care they received. Leah and I are even considering making them our primary care as well. God truly cares about the practical details of life.

Praises
• Pastor Stephen Rogers from Harvest Baptist Church in Hagerstown, MD, gifted us a bilingual Bible. We have been using it constantly as Leah and I continue working to learn Spanish. It has been an incredible help.
• Over the past two months, we have picked up four new supporting churches, bringing us to approximately 25% of our needed support. We are so thankful!
• The Hammonds (who will be joining us in planting City Baptist Church) have made a strong push in growing the Bible study they've started. It is exciting to see early groundwork being laid.

Prayer Requests
• A potential building opportunity in Bridgeport — pray for clear direction and open doors.
• I am going to be taking Pastor Pete Montoro's inner-city church planting class in Astoria, Queens. Please pray the Lord would continue shaping and growing me through this training.
• Continued monthly financial support as we press toward full support.
• That the Holy Spirit would even now prepare hearts in Bridgeport for the gospel.
• Strength, unity, and wisdom for our family during this season of travel and preparation.

Thank you for standing with us. Your prayers, encouragement, and support mean more than you know. We are reminded constantly that we are not doing this alone — we are sent, and we are supported by faithful churches like yours.

Until all hear,
Anthony & Leah Frazer
Adalee (2) & Anthony III (6 months)
Church Planters to Bridgeport, CT
City Baptist Church

letters.title: June 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Dear supporting church,

We have been reminded on our deputation trail of the need that there is in the big cities of not just the United States, but also all over the world. God has given us opportunities to go to Houston, Dallas/Fort Worth, Philadelphia, and New York City. These are some of the largest cities in the United States, and many of them have very few churches. Many Christians want to move away from the places to escape the evil that resides in them, but how will they ever have light if we who possess it leave? Seeing these cities has only increased the burden in our heart to reach the city that God has called us to. It is alarming the amount of people who are left unreached in the big cities of the world.

In May and June, we have been in the Northeast presenting our ministry to churches. With it being my first time in the Northeast, it has been a blessing to meet many new pastors and churches and to see their hearts for their cities. We have been in western New York for most of the time. Daci's sister and brother-in-law live near Buffalo, New York and he is the pastor of a church in the area. We have enjoyed the time spent with family when we are not presenting and spending time with other pastors.

We praise the Lord that we have been promised 23% of our needed support in just three months. The Lord has been good to us in giving us meetings, providing our needs, and protecting us as we travel many miles. Thank you for your faithful prayers and support.

Your missionaries,
The Scotts

missionaries.prayer: Pray for Matthew's health as doctors work to diagnose and manage a rare, worsening skin condition, for safe travel back to Point Hope through Arctic storms, and for continued provision as the family looks at repairs to their home and the church building.

letters.title: February Update
letters.excerpt:
February 1st, 2026

Happy New Year! We hope you all had a great Christmas and New Year! It was so nice to spend Christmas as a family together on the mission field! We've been on the mission field of Point Hope now for ten years by God's grace! We cannot thank you enough for all your prayers and support over this decade, we couldn't have done it without you all! Lord willing, if the Lord tarries, we will still be out here another ten years! Of course we are praying that this would be the year that our Lord Jesus comes to take us home!

We've had some bad weather lately with the wind chills down to negative fifty degrees and blowing snow causing big snow drifts. The church pipes froze up a couple times so we are trying to keep those thawed the best we can. We may need to look into insulating it better in the summer. I'm also praying about having metal siding put onto our house. With the harsh winters I believe this will help protect and prolong our house. The guys that did such a great job on our addition measured everything when they were here, we just need wisdom about having it done this summer or next depending on our finances.

Unfortunately I am currently writing this prayer letter in Seattle once again for medical reasons. My symptoms that I've been dealing with have gotten much worse, as I currently have six more of those ulcerating sores that keep getting bigger and deeper every day. I was supposed to see the dermatologist at the end of February but the sores have gotten to be unbearable, so the doctors told me to come to Seattle as soon as possible. So far they have taken two more biopsies as well as blood work and two CT scans. They still are not one hundred percent sure what it is but they have an idea. They believe it's a very rare condition that they have admitted the medical field needs about fifty more years to fully understand. Thank God I know the Great Physician who knows all about it! Tomorrow I will pick up the medication they have prescribed me that they are hoping will heal up the sores. They say that more sores can appear at any moment and I will most likely have to deal with this for the rest of my life since they haven't found a cure for it yet. I sure would appreciate your prayers that these sores would be manageable, if it be God's will!

I am scheduled to fly back to Point Hope on February 3rd and arrive on the 4th. There is a storm brewing in the arctic once again, so I sure would appreciate your prayers that I can fly in and not get stuck in Kotzebue, which is the village we have to take a bush plane from. I'm so looking forward to getting back with my family again and ministering together for the Lord where He has called us! Thank you again for all you do for us!! God bless!

Your Missionaries to Point Hope, Alaska,
Matthew, Jennifer, Jacob, Joanna, Sarah, and Julia Sutton

letters.title: May / June Update
letters.excerpt:
FULL SPEED AHEAD

The months of May and June were filled with opportunities to serve the Lord as our family traveled over 5,300 miles throughout Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, and Missouri. We are continually amazed at the doors God continues to open and are grateful for every church that has allowed us to minister alongside them.

Some of the highlights of these past two months included preaching in Linton, Indiana, being encouraged by the kindness of God's people in Bedford, Indiana, spending time with a faithful church in Robins, Iowa, and conducting several Bible Handouts, including one in Lemont, Illinois. We also had the privilege of participating in missions conferences in Springfield, Illinois, and Highland, Indiana, where we were able to share the burden God has given us to help churches reach America through the Bible Handout Ministry.

One of our favorite stops was spending more than a week with Whetstone Baptist Church in Mountain Grove, Missouri. During our time there, I had the opportunity to preach, help build a new church website, and enjoy wonderful fellowship with Pastor Sousley and his family. We also enjoyed a special time of ministry in Scottsburg, Indiana, before concluding the month of June in Wildwood, Missouri, where we helped with Teen Blast and Vacation Bible School.

The Lord also greatly blessed the Bible Handout Ministry during these two months. Through six organized Bible Handouts, we distributed approximately 130 Bibles, gave 45 clear Gospel presentations, and rejoiced as 25 people trusted Christ as their Saviour. It is exciting to watch churches catch the vision of putting God's Word directly into the hands of people throughout their communities.

The Lord has continued to provide for our ministry, and we are thankful to report that our support level has now reached 65%. We are grateful for the churches that continue to pray for us, support us, and allow us to partner with them in reaching America with the Gospel.

PRAYER REQUESTS
1. The Lord to provide our remaining support by the end of the year
2. Wisdom as we seek the Lord's provision for an RV motorhome
3. Haddon's upcoming doctor's appointment and continued good health
4. Our family as we continue adjusting to full-time travel with three young children
5. Continued open doors for Bible Handouts, soulwinning training, and souls saved

THANK YOU
Thank you again for your faithful prayers and partnership in the ministry. We want to support you as much as you support us!

YOUR SERVANTS
Andrew, Abby, Alexis, Haddon & Joslyn Rardin

letters.title: February 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
February was a busy month for us. The Lord provided a way for us to make a short trip to America and back for Aly's father's wedding. It was a good trip that brought opportunity to see both of our families, but it did bring some challenge as well. Cassian got sick during our trip, which made traveling back to Japan much more difficult as you could probably imagine. He had a stomach bug, then on top of that during our travel back to Japan, we all caught a cold. We were forced to take a week of break when we got back. We are thankful that it was a smaller sickness, but it was our first time going through that with a baby, and adding a flight to America and back definitely added to the difficulty of it all. Over all of that we are thankful for the Lord's grace and provision. We were able to use the trip as an opportunity to get gifts for a few different families around town and have good conversations about our trip. We have been able to have much longer conversations with the Mori family. They own the Teshio Food Center, a small grocery store and bento kitchen. We have been talking with the owners of a restaurant in the road station on the main road that runs through Teshio. They are the Tamada family, an older couple that loves to talk with Cassian. We do our best to talk as much as we can, and pray the Lord opens a door for us to invite them to a church service or event as the restaurant is not open on Sundays. We also have been getting closer to the Yamano family. Aly met the wife, Yui, at the hospital a couple of months ago. Yui wanted to be friends with Aly because she has a baby that's close to Cassian's age, and wants to learn more about English and America. We have been able to have dinner with them a few times already. Please pray for them, as Yui and her husband are both open to learn more about the Bible. Our constant prayer is that the Lord uses the relationships we build to further the Gospel in their hearts, whether through being invited to church, or by being a witness of Christ's love. We came back to a surprising amount of nice weather in Teshio.

We are told it is a very unusual winter this year. The feet of snow usually stick around until closer to the end of March, but a few days after we got back most of the snow on the ground has melted, and there is not expected to be much more snow coming for the rest of the winter. The Lord has definitely given an easy transition to living here, which we are thankful for. Since the New Year we have taken time to hold Sunday School before our morning service, with an initial goal to give us some practical training in reading translated Bible stories, running crafts in Japanese, and learning Sunday School songs in Japanese. We are excited to be pushed in our Japanese learning in a practical and spiritual sense. Aly and Cassian are especially looking forward to next month, as they will have the opportunity to meet more moms in town, with a few events for moms and babies happening, so we ask that you would pray that she will be able to converse with them well, and that Cassian gets along with the other little ones. We appreciate your prayers as we head into our unexpected early spring. We are looking for more opportunities to meet more people and be a witness to more people in our area.

letters.title: March 2026 Update
letters.excerpt: Spring has come early here in North Hokkaido, and that has allowed us opportunities to continue meeting people in town. Even though we have been here for 6 months, our faces are still fresh in the community. With the warmer weather, there are more activities around town. Even when there aren't scheduled activities, we take the chance to walk around town as a family. Our family "sanpo," or leisurely strolls, oftentimes turn into conversations with other people that are out and about. We praise the Lord for Cassian oftentimes being our ice breaker to get a conversation started. Aly and Cassian have been meeting different mothers and babies around town, and Aly has even started to have a Japanese and English study time every Wednesday with two other Japanese mothers. She prays for it to be a time of not just study, but also a time for witnessing. We ask for prayer for the Lord's wisdom always in knowing how to be the right witness to the people that we meet and interact with on a daily basis. We are praising the Lord with provision for the process of getting our Japanese driver's licenses. The last couple of months, we had to wait for some extra paperwork involving my American driver's license. All I needed for my license was a record for how long I had an American driver's license, and that took a very long time to get from the Iowa DOT. In the Lord's timing however, we got the paperwork here, and sent it off. It has now been approved, and we are waiting for a date to be arranged for us to take our written exam. Please pray for our study, as Japan has recently made it a much more difficult test. We ask prayer for these areas as well as future ministry and outreach opportunities that we will have throughout this year. We are thankful for you all, and look forward to see how the Lord continues to use us here in Teshio.

letters.title: April 2026 Update
letters.excerpt: We praise the Lord as the last two months have been very busy. As April approached we excitedly prepared for Resurrection Sunday. We had been praying that the Lord would bring visitors to this special service. There have been multiple families that we have been building relationships with, and we had earnestly prayed that they would attend. Aly invited her friend's family, which brought an encouraging result. The Lord has opened the door for us to interact frequently with the whole family, having dinner together, playing games, and even practicing English and Japanese together. They had said that all four of them would be at church for Easter. That morning, their baby was sick, which we expected would cause them all to stay home. Yet the father and daughter still attended the service. We were very encouraged that he would still come to church even though his wife and baby stayed home. We are daily in prayer that they would accept Christ. After Easter, we started planning for Jadon's family to make a visit. We also started the process of taking our driving exams, which would happen one right after the other. The studying and planning caused April to go by fast, and soon came May.

letters.title: May 2026 Update
letters.excerpt: We praise the Lord for allowing us to stay so connected to our family even though we are on the other side of the globe. We also praise the Lord for allowing them to be able to come visit us. It was a good time together to be able to not only show them Japan, but also show the mission field and the ministry that we are a part of. During our family's visit, Mother's Day happened, which gave us another event to invite people around town to attend church. There was a mother and her two daughters that came to the service after we invited her. The Lord has been allowing us to be connected with more and more people around our town. We pray that we can continue to be a light in Teshio. We have started and are in the process of getting our driver's licenses. It definitely has been quite the process. We took our written exam after our family left Japan. Recently, Japan changed the requirements for foreigners to get a Japanese driver's license. For the written exam there are 50 questions and you can only get 3 wrong. We were praying that at least one of us would pass on the first attempt. Praise the Lord, He answered our prayer! Aly passed the written exam and I will take it again on June 9th. Please pray that I can pass on this next attempt, so we can move forward in setting up and taking the driving exam. To finish out the month, I was given the opportunity to volunteer at the elementary school to help each grade plant flowers in the school flower bed. A friend of mine, who works at the schools, said that the staff appreciated my help and that I left a good impression. We pray that I will have more opportunities to volunteer and further be a light in the community. We look forward to the summer season where many events around town occur. We ask for prayer as we seek to bring the Gospel to our town, Teshio.

letters.title: January / February 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Greetings Pastor and Church Family

A new year brings new adventures. The realities of traveling full-time are beginning to set in, but we're excited about all the new experiences we'll have this year. Although we won't submit our visa applications until the end of the year, we've spoken to our sponsor and are starting to gather the necessary documents. We've also just sent off for all the kids' passports, which has made things feel more real.

Wow! 29 Percent

We've been traveling for almost six months now, and we're incredibly grateful for the hospitality and generosity of those we've met along the way. While the winter weather in January necessitated some scheduling changes, we're once again able to witness God's guidance in every part of our adventure. He provided us with a comfortable and cozy place to relax and cherish the moment with family, while also keeping us safe as we resumed traveling.

We praise the Lord for the many meetings we have scheduled. However, we humbly ask your prayers that we will be able to fill a few openings in our schedule during our time in the northwest in July.

Will you pray with us?
- Please pray for our safety on the roads and for good health as we visit numerous churches.
- Please pray for us as we seek to learn Italian.
- Please pray for God's swift support so we can reach the Italian mission field soon.
- Please also pray for the hearts of the Italian people, that God may prepare them for His message.

letters.title: March / April 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Greetings Pastor and Church Family

One of the choices that everyone, particularly missionaries on deputation, must make daily and in every circumstance is to praise the Lord. While there is always something to complain about, there is also always something to praise God about. God has been teaching us to choose praising God during this busy time on the road.

43 Percent and Counting

March and April have been our mission conference months. We attended services 33 days out of the 61 days in March and April. There have been times we have woken up trying to figure out where we are and what the day holds. Nevertheless, despite the demanding schedule, God has blessed us, and we are grateful for the opportunity to share the burden entrusted to us for the country of Italy.

We had a close scare this week. A wire in our side panel overheated and burned the connector, almost causing a fire. Smoke billowed out of the panel, but thankfully, it wasn't worse.

We are heading to the West Coast for the summer. Looking forward to seeing friends and family out there.

Will you pray with us?
- Please pray for our safety on the roads and for good health as we visit numerous churches.
- Please pray for us as we seek to learn Italian.
- Please pray for God's swift support so we can reach the Italian mission field soon.
- Please also pray for the hearts of the Italian people, that God may prepare them for His message.

letters.title: May / June 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Greetings Pastor and Church Family

Deputation is truly a journey of faith. We've been traveling for 10 months and have been without a permanent home for a year. It's easy to take the security and comfort of your own place for granted, especially when you're constantly packing and unpacking. But this is where God strengthens our faith in Him.

Serving God is an honor, but it is also a walk of faith.

We Made It Halfway! 50%

We've spent May and June exploring the West, visiting New Mexico, Arizona, California, Oregon, and now Washington. This is our first time out west, and it's been an incredible adventure. We've had the privilege of witnessing some magnificent national parks along the way, which have humbled us and reminded us of the Majesty of God.

Additionally, we've had the opportunity to spend quality time with our extended family. Being a part of their world for a few weeks has strengthened our connection and brought us closer together.

We have been in 17 churches and traveled 4,874 miles.

God has been good to us and we are so thankful for His protection and provision. Onward to the second half!

Will you pray with us?
- Please pray for our safety on the roads and for good health as we visit numerous churches.
- Please pray for us as we seek to learn Italian.
- Please pray for God's swift support so we can reach the Italian mission field soon.
- Please also pray for the hearts of the Italian people, that God may prepare them for His message.

letters.title: May 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
May Prayer Letter

The last couple months have been busy, but they have been so exciting. I was able to go to a camp in a nearby area and preach. It was a huge blessing. During that camp many teens were saved and surrendered to God. After that we had the opportunity to join the VBS here. Before VBS, my wife and I were talking and mentioned that I thought it would be good for her to try and witness to some of the kids in Bisaya during VBS. At first, I could tell she was nervous and unsure, but on Thursday she got her first opportunity to witness. The funny thing was that the first girl only spoke English and all the other workers were nervous about witnessing in English so they sent her to my wife. The next girl that my wife got to witness to spoke a tiny bit of English, but mainly understood and spoke Bisaya. So my wife slowly went through the Gospel, hoping the girl would understand. It was amazing how God works, because the girl's heart was so open and ready. When my wife was asking her questions to make sure she understood the Gospel and verses she had just read, it was very obvious that she understood and wanted to accept Christ into her heart. My wife had several opportunities to witness to kids that same day and the next. It was so exciting for me to see. I'm so proud of my wife for letting God use her in that way. The language learning process has been very difficult, because pretty much as soon as we arrived in the Philippines she got pregnant, then had our daughter. It is often hard for her as she gets little sleep some nights and then first thing in the morning has language school. Although it has been hard, it is worth all the time and effort to see people saved and their lives touched by our God.

We will be coming back to the states for a short furlough and are so excited to see many of you and tell you about what God is doing in the lives of the people here. The plan is to come back in October-March. Please pray for us as we prepare everything for coming back to the states.

Prayer Request:
1. God to give us more opportunities to reach people here with the Gospel.
2. God's guidance on where He wants us to plant a church here.
3. That we would get approved for our permanent visas.

Blessings:
1. Lots of teens and kids saved.
2. Opportunities to be involved in summer camps, VBS, and other ministries.
3. God using my wife to witness to kids and her growth in the language.

God Bless,
Austin and Rhadee Cowling

letters.title: January Update 2026
letters.excerpt:
Dear Pastor,

What a privilege to serve the Lord here in Guam. It's amazing to think that God would let all of us be co-laborers with Christ in the ministry of the Lord.

Reflecting over the past few months and looking towards the New Year, I am reminded of the goodness and grace of the Lord.

We baptized nine last Sunday in Tumon Bay. Thank the Lord for the warm waters of the Pacific in this region! We had over thirty visitors attend the baptism. While I was giving the gospel, several tourists wandered by and heard the message. What an opportunity!

On New Year's Eve, four of our young men preached. During that service, a twenty-eight year old man was saved. Please pray for our young preachers. Our youth are a blessing! They continue to be the backbone of our Bible Club ministry which reaches all over this island. Twenty-two of our teenagers are currently involved in this ministry.

Sherry continues to cook meals and offer hospitality every Sunday afternoon for the military. Navy, Air Force, Marine, and Army personnel have been to our house for food and fellowship. We absolutely love these folks! My respect is to those who have raised their hands and "signed on the dotted line" as a willing sacrifice for our country. PCS season is here as four of our families and several of our singles will be headed to other places of military service. The Lord has allowed two families to join in the last three weeks. The rotation continues.

Our international meal next week will reflect the diversity in our church. We will enjoy Filipino, Micronesian, Chamorro, and other Asian foods, along with a big pot of Louisiana gumbo.

The church plant in Yona continues to grow and prosper. In two weeks, we look forward to some extensive door-knocking in the area. Pray for the work in Yona.

The Lord is good to us! We praise the Lord for the good health that He has given us to get His work accomplished.

Steven Barnes,
Missionary to Guam

missionaries.prayer: Pray for the Kitchens as they minister to a constantly rotating military congregation, for the Odom family as they walk through Kyle's cancer diagnosis, and for continued fruit as new servicemen and women pass through Grace Baptist Church.
missionaries.name: Rob & Daci Kitchen

letters.title: July 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Dear fellow laborers in Christ,

What a joy and privilege it is to serve the King of kings and Lord of lords! Our theme at Grace Baptist Church is, "Mine Eyes Have Seen the King" from Isaiah 6:5. What a life-changing moment it was for the prophet to see his Holy God high and lifted up upon His throne. Imagine how it could change your life if our "Eyes Would See the King!"

We have had an eventful and busy quarter since our last letter. We have experienced the largest personnel transition that we have seen since being in Germany. The nature of military ministry is that we have people but for a short amount of time. Because of that, there are a lot of "welcomes" and a lot of "farewells." It is challenging, but the Lord is so gracious and wonderful to allow us the time that we have with the people He brings in our path. We said farewell to two pillar families of GBC these past two months: the Lacroix family and the Edwards Knode family. Both have been with us their entire time in Germany. Both families were faithful servants of the Lord! Both were families that God used to help me grow as a pastor. I am thankful for the impact these two families had here and will continue to have as they serve the Lord at the next place!

In May, I made a very quick trip back to the U.S. at the request of a former family of our church. All three of the teenagers were saved at GBC and God grew them tremendously while they were here. Since leaving, the husband, Kyle, was diagnosed with a very aggressive cancer. In May he wasn't given much time to live and the family requested if I could come and see him. The Lord provided and enabled me to make a trip to San Antonio to minister to this dear family and speak to Kyle about eternity one last time. He gave a clear testimony of being saved and knew that the Lord was going to protect and provide for his family in his absence. It was the hardest moment I think I have faced in the ministry. While there was an assurance from the entire family of God's promise to believers of Heaven, it was difficult seeing this family walk through the valley of death. God's grace IS SUFFICIENT and was sweet in those moments of tears, laughter, jokes, stories, and prayers. Please pray for the Odom family as God leads them through this difficult time.

There are many moments in ministry that I would consider highlights but there is nothing like the saving of a soul and seeing believers grow in their relationship with the Lord through their obedience to Him. What makes that even more memorable is when it is your own children. In December of 2024, Amelia spoke with my wife about being saved and put her faith in Jesus to save her on Christmas Eve, Hallelujah! There have been a few times we have talked to her about being baptized and she has had a great understanding of baptism but has had a great fear of being in front of people and a slight fear of water. Last week, after seeing her friend baptized, she asked about it again. We spent some time reviewing what baptism was and she was determined, fear of people and water or not, that she needed to be baptized. July 12, 2026, I had the privilege as Amelia's pastor and her dad, to baptize her as she committed to obey God and live for Him. What a joy it was to be used of God to be involved in the life of my own children that way! We greatly rejoice for every soul that is saved, baptized and lives to please God.

Thank you for loving our family and partnering with us to reach our military servicemen and women. We couldn't do what God has called us to do without your sacrifice and help. What God does here will be fruit to your account! We love you!

The Kitchen Family

letters.title: June 2026 Update Letter
letters.excerpt:
Dear supporting Pastors and friends,

After 19 years of teaching at a public high school, I've officially resigned on June 26 to become a full-time pastor! Your financial support and prayers are going to make possible a prayer we've had for many years.

The month of June was filled with several blessings that I'd like to share. First, our church held several days of fasting and prayer, specifically focused on the men in our church under spiritual attack. Although we haven't seen any dramatic changes or improvements, we have seen God helping one of the men in great ways. Progress is being made behind the scenes in his life and this is encouraging news for me.

For Father's Day, the ladies of our church planned a special church luncheon in honor of dads, filled with great food and fun activities. At the end of the month, I was also able to celebrate my 14th wedding anniversary. I'm thankful for one of the sisters at our church who was able to watch our kids and let us enjoy a special day together.

In a previous prayer letter, I had mentioned that I was able to witness to the father of one of our young men. Salvador has, sadly, passed into eternity from health complications. But I'm glad to know he heard the gospel message before dying. His son, Salvatore, seems to be holding up well. But we're praying for God to help him with the next steps of his life. He needs gainful employment and help finding a new place to live. He needs to move out of the 2-bedroom apartment he is in, for a 1-bedroom. We hope he can find something close to church so that he can stay consistent in attendance and growth.

Next month (July) we're having a special Spiritual Wellness conference with Bro. Jamie Jett as our main speaker. We're really looking forward to hearing some great preaching and to be recharged after so many ups and downs we've had. Please pray that God would bless this conference in a special way.

Prayer Requests:
1. We still need Sign Language interpreters
2. Please pray for repentance and restitution of a disciplined member
3. Pray for more souls to be reached with the gospel

missionaries.prayer: Pray for God's protection and provision as the Dorrs finish roofing the church and house in Vicam, for Bro. Federico's health and continued faithfulness, and for the children's home now fully equipped with mattresses.
missionaries.name: Micah & Jillian Dorr

letters.title: July 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Dear Pastor and Church,

I hope you are having a wonderful summer! We are immensely enjoying the change of pace. Most days start out extremely hot, but in the afternoon the clouds roll in and often bring some much-anticipated rain. Just about every evening, the students and teens finish an activity or church service, then start up a game of soccer and play until close to midnight. We have been seeing people trust in Jesus in just about every service recently. God is good!

Bro. Federico: We have been taking up bucket offerings for our upcoming VBS recently. On Wednesday, Bro. Federico caught my eye as he wheeled his wheelchair to the front to participate in the offering. Bro. Federico is blind and has had both of his legs amputated. About a year and a half ago, he was crossing the road in his village when a driver didn't see him and ran him over. His hip was broken, adding to his pain. Despite these difficulties, no one is as faithful to church as Bro. Federico. He is my cheerleading section on the front row, always with an encouraging "Amen!" It brought tears to my eyes as he gave what I'm sure was most of his money in the offering. Heaven will be a sweet place for Federico!

Vicam: Last month we were able to pour the floor for the church in Vicam. God has provided in a special way for the metal roof. On Monday, we will take a group of guys up there and hope to finish the roofs on both the church and the house in two days. As soon as the roof is on, Bro. Emir is planning to combine two of the Bible studies into one service at the church while continuing to hold a service across town. Please pray for God's protection and provision. I'm so excited about what God is doing!

Thank you so much for your amazing generosity in helping buy the mattresses for the children's home. We were able to get everything we needed!

Your Servants,
Micah and Jillian Dorr

letters.title: April 2026 Update
letters.excerpt:
Dear Praying friends,

Bless the LORD O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name (Psalm 103:1)! I look forward to the opportunity quarterly to write and send our prayer letter. First, because God continues to be incredibly good to us. Second, because we love each of you and can never thank you enough for partnering in prayer and support for us and with us. And last, because I am confident many of you will take our new prayer requests and pray with us. THANK YOU!

Two highlights come to mind in sharing some of the blessings from the first quarter of this year. The first is our first international Gospel Crusade in Lima, Peru. Over thirty people came from six different churches around America to help us. We rejoice that over 200 people trusted Christ as Saviour during our week-long campaign! There were so many blessings; I would be glad to send a video that my home church made if you would like to see it.

The second highlight is that I had the wonderful privilege to be a part of two of my sons' ordinations in the past couple months. I rejoice in being a part of young preachers' ordinations, but to preach two of my sons' ordinations was truly a highlight of my entire ministry. My wife and I are humbled at God's goodness and grace.

SPECIFIC PRAYER REQUESTS:
1. New England Gospel Initiative - We began this major project here in April. Please pray specifically for churches to get on board to be committed to WEEKLY door-to-door evangelism. Please pray for the college men evangelism internship starting in the middle of May. Please pray for the plan to go to churches around New England and commit to soulwinning to encourage and help churches.
2. New England Baptist Teen Camp - June 22-26, we will be having our 15th annual NEBTC! Brother Caleb Garraway will be our main speaker. Please pray that God will work mightily in the lives of the precious young people of the Northeast.
3. Two Grandsons - health - Please continue to pray for Andrew and Lucas and their incredible health challenges. Every church we go to, people remind us of their love and prayers. That encourages us more than you know.
4. Bridgeport Gospel Crusade - August 17-21, we will be having our next Gospel Crusade. A location for the tent crusade is our greatest need, along with additional finances, housing for those who come and help, and for churches around Connecticut and the rest of New England to come labor with us.
5. NEW NEED - Travel trailer/fifth wheel - We are at the place in our ministry that we desperately need a travel trailer that we can use for many people around the country that are coming to help us with our Crusades and Gospel Initiative. If you know of one in good condition, or would be interested in helping us purchase one, please let me know.

Servant and friend,

John Barnes
Evangelist
